1446536480957030400 [2021-10-08] @DanielleFong 💜 1614 🔁 390
when i was a kid reading encyclopedias and astrophysics books for educated amateurs (‘cause that’s what i wanted to read…) i arrived in kindergarten where we were literally learning letters from the alphabet one by one
it was kafkaesque torture & my teacher called me a smartass https://t.co/3HYognDwhk
  [Quoting Tweet 1446435627495530496 (missing)]
↓
1446536848998899712 [2021-10-08] @DanielleFong 💜 331 🔁 4
i think it was my parents who insisted they test me, and through whatever test they did which if i remember properly included analogies, geometry stuff with blocks, and like, make a story out of pictures as well as some math, they were like, ok you tested into the 11th grade
↓
1446537241287970818 [2021-10-08] @DanielleFong 💜 231 🔁 3
but talented and gifted programs were eliminated then. every class from what was then second grade and up had a gifted stream. none of the kindergarten and first grade classes did. they stuck me in first grade…
↓
1446537611246505986 [2021-10-08] @DanielleFong 💜 226 🔁 1
ultimately i’m grateful for the friends i made in the class I ended up in. there were still bright kids in class who it was really fun to hang out with, and a statistically unusual number of my classmates have gotten phds or gone on to pretty deep research…
↓
1446538041175248912 [2021-10-08] @DanielleFong 💜 231 🔁 1
and probably (surely??) just plunking me directly into the 11th grade would have been hilariously suboptimal.

can you imagine? it has been done though, i guess.

school was fine as long as i could do whatever i wanted, so long as the work got done. i’d be reading or drawing…
↓
1446538602108932097 [2021-10-08] @DanielleFong 💜 218 🔁 2
or talking, quietly, with one of my friends, one of the cleverer or funnier people in class.

at one point i was drawing up, kind of, machine geometries for imagined fusion reactors. there was a spelling test and they were like “spelling test” and i said “can’t you see i’m busy”
↓
1446538988496596993 [2021-10-08] @DanielleFong 💜 200 🔁 1
they let me get away with it. and the class kept going

in jr high, it was not good. the social scene blew up / collapsed as people moved away and new schools merged, and i had a punitive teacher who really hated being corrected or asked questions. she kept giving me detention…
↓
1446539288548675586 [2021-10-08] @DanielleFong 💜 163 🔁 1
actually it wasn’t just me. she had tenure, and she was infamous. she would give so much detention that the detention population would exceed her home room population. she would give detention to people in the hallway walking to class.
↓
1446539647987986437 [2021-10-08] @DanielleFong 💜 172 🔁 1
anyway, after the nth time this happened, i was like, this is bullshit, i’m locked in here, but i wonder if the doors are actually physically unlocked. so i waited till she was distracted and then slipped out, and checked the doors. they were unlocked! i bolted, hid behind a tree
↓
1446540043892449284 [2021-10-08] @DanielleFong 💜 198 🔁 1 [(SEED) type=semantic_search]
and then walked home.

my parents, ex world traveling hippies, did not send me back. they decided i didn’t have to, i was ahead a year anyway, and that i was just going to school for recess (for friends, essentially), anyway, a function it no longer provided
↓
1446540621037154306 [2021-10-08] @DanielleFong 💜 176 🔁 1
at some point we found out that the tests they had been hiding from a couple weeks before i quit said i was in the 99.97th percentile as scored for uni entrants, or whatever, so we were like, huh, maybe i should just go to university
i was too young for the GED, but not the SAT!
↓
1446540779195928602 [2021-10-08] @DanielleFong 💜 152 🔁 1
before that, school was books, essays, horseback riding, 3d modeling and programming class at the community college. and lots of videogames; even making some with map editors and engines, little things
↓
1446541148261060613 [2021-10-08] @DanielleFong 💜 309 🔁 15
i can’t imagine the level of checked out i would be if i had to suffer through 7-12 at the traditional pace. it is almost unimaginable. like a prison type experience, maybe.

this is literally the time you have maximum neurons and are pruning them, and synapses. use it or lose it
↓
1446541547936354326 [2021-10-08] @DanielleFong 💜 879 🔁 119
the brain damage inflicted on young people who are forced to waste their talents on doing the exact same thing as their age peers at the same rate is unimaginable. it is maybe the costliest thing that we do to human capital.

and the fact is everyone has talents & interests
├── 1446541887838556169 [2021-10-08] @DanielleFong 💜 350 🔁 25
│   remote school *could have been* and should have been an opening up of education into a lifelong process of pursuing one’s interests, refining one’s skills, and learning about the world around you
│   
│   instead, zoom and ai enabled cameras monopolized your attention & gaze. even worse!
│   ↓
│   1446542192546402308 [2021-10-08] @DanielleFong 💜 332 🔁 17
│   we had a pandemic before, you know, the schooling solution was books, and outdoor classes when the weather abided. (and sweaters!)
│   
│   i honestly fucking weep for this generation. they have all of this technology and it is being put to use melting their brains.
│   ↓
│   1446542563121500173 [2021-10-08] @DanielleFong 💜 322 🔁 20
│   the quicker people build lifelong education into a parallel system you can seriously opt-in to in lieu of the mainline k-12-college-grad school legible education, the better. i am starting to feel like it is pretty mission critical; like education is getting profoundly bad
│   ↓
│   1446547351003439105 [2021-10-08] @DanielleFong 💜 175 🔁 2
│   a badge system wherein you are a proven badass in projects of certain categories, like earning your Jump Wings as a parachutist
│   ↓
│   1446654924280975364 [2021-10-09] @DanielleFong 💜 180 🔁 1
│   people complaining this thread is boring, Sorry! it was not intended to go viral. 
│   
│   just thought it would be a good time to talk about something i had experienced. i am sensitive to when learning resources are shut down, but maybe things are still ok (?) in the NYC schoolsystem🤷🏻‍♀️
│   ↓

rating.reasoning_summary: This strand represents fragmented thematic drift around education dissatisfaction, lacking a clear boundary object or evolutionary arc. While Danielle Fong's 2021 thread provides a compelling personal narrative about escaping traditional schooling (the only substantive node), the surrounding tweets are disconnected vignettes: homeschooling trends during COVID, vacation logistics, parenting complaints, and random life updates. There is no dialectical engagement—no one builds on Fong's ideas, proposes alternatives, or creates shared vocabulary. The 'strand' is an illusion created by keyword overlap ('school,' 'parents,' 'kids') rather than narrative coherence. Utility is minimal: Fong's story offers anecdotal validation for homeschooling but no actionable framework, and the other tweets contribute nothing beyond ambient cultural noise.

essential_tweets.annotation: Origin: Fong's critique of kindergarten as 'Kafkaesque torture' for gifted kids
Context: Elimination of gifted programs forced grade-level placement
Catalyst: Parents pull her from school after detention abuse
Alternative path: Homeschooling leads to early university entry via SAT
Core argument: Traditional pacing is 'prison-like' during peak neuroplasticity
Key claim: Age-based schooling is 'costliest thing we do to human capital'
Proposed solution: Parallel lifelong education system with opt-in credentialing
Concrete example: Badge system for project-based competency (like Jump Wings)
Weak pre-context: COVID driving homeschooling consideration (no follow-up)
Tangential signal: Parent prioritizing adult vacation over child 'education' travel
